title: Supreme Court Declines to Interfere With Rs 14.49 Crore Arbitral Award in Sourav Ganguly's Favour
case_name: Percept Talent Management Pvt. Ltd. v. Sourav Ganguly
card_summary: The Supreme Court dismissed Percept Talent Management's challenge to a Rs 14.49 crore arbitral award in Sourav Ganguly's favour, declining to interfere with the Calcutta High Court's order upholding it. Percept had sought to terminate its 2003 management agreement over Ganguly's absence from the Indian team, but the tribunal found that right was never exercised in time and stood waived.
card_tip: A termination right tied to a time condition can be lost through delay and continued conduct under the contract; invoking it years later will not revive it.
verification_notes: Confirmed across Bar and Bench, LiveLaw and Exchange4Media; all agree on the award amount, the waiver finding on the termination clause, and the Calcutta High Court's April 2026 order being upheld. Minor variations in how outlets describe the interest computation are omitted from the card.
